info.title: Vision Board API
info.summary: The one board API, for the page, agents and the vb CLI
info.description: Every operation on the project ledger, defined once. The MCP tools and `vb` commands are generated from the operations marked `x-agent: true`; the route table is generated from this document.

get.description: List every board in the project with its title and its own last ledger line. Call it first to find the board id the other operations take in their path. It takes no input. It returns `boards` (each with `board`, `title` and `seq`, the board's latest ledger line) and `head`, the ledger's latest line number. Reads need no credentials.

boards.title: Where Vision Board goes from here

get.summary: Read a board as it is now
get.description: Read one board as it is now: the full View (regions, nodes and links, meaning only, no coordinates), the person's answers on every node, each node's latest version, and `head`. On a board agents write to, it also carries the open grant requests (`requests`) and each region's holders (`holders`), both left out when empty. Pass the board id. Use it to see the whole board before you draw on it; use `show_node` for one node's history. `state` and `versions` are keyed by node id, the string form of the node number.

put.summary: Create or rename a board, as the person
put.description: Create a board, or rename one, as the person: `title` and an optional `summary` (left out, the summary is cleared). A new board id creates the board, with no agent creator, so every agent must ask for it with `request_grant` before writing on it; an existing id renames that board. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the stored ledger line.

200.description: The board was renamed: the stored line.

201.description: The board was created: the stored line.

get.summary: Read one node with its history
get.description: Read one node with every version it has had, the person's notes, replies, proposals, the park bundle if there is one, its links, its container (`region`) and the person's size. Pass the board id and the node number `n`. Add `linked=true` to also get the nodes linked to it, one hop away. Use it before you answer a comment or redraw a node, so you build on the latest version.

get.description: List the items on a board that the person has not decided yet. Each item gives its latest `ver` and `status`, whether it is `pending` your answer (a comment or "needs context" nobody has answered, or moved to Later with no park bundle), and whether it is `unseen` (a newer version than the person last saw). Pass the board id. With your Bearer secret the list covers only the containers you hold, so you are never told to answer another agent's items.

Read what the person did on a board after a ledger position, including the answers to your grant requests. Pass `after`, the `head` you last saw (0 for everything), and optionally `limit` and `wait` (0-60 seconds) to hold the call until the person presses Send or answers a request. A wait that times out returns `{ responses: [], head }`. A note is reported as the `comment` or `context` act that made it, carrying the note's latest text and kind, again whenever the person edits it; a note removed before you could see it never appears, and a `note-remove` appears only for a note you may already have read. The server keeps no state for you: pass back the `head` you got. `more: true` means read again at once. With your Bearer secret the answer covers only the containers you hold.

Read raw ledger lines after a position, oldest first, from every writer. Pass `after` (a `seq`, 0 for the start), `limit` (default 100, at most 500) and optionally `board` to keep only one board's lines. It returns JSON `{ events, head, more? }`, or just the lines as `application/jsonl` when you ask for that; a jsonl reader pages by the last line's `seq` and stops on an empty page. Use `check_responses` instead when you only want the person's answers.

post.description: Join the project as an agent and get your agent id and secret, once. Pass a short `label` such as "Pricing chat". Joining grants nothing: you may draw a new board of your own; for a board another agent made, call `request_grant` with just its `board` first. Save `agent` and `secret` in your durable notes now, because a context compaction loses them and the secret cannot be read again; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` on your writes. If a write answers `not-authenticated`, join again and ask for your grants again. This is the one write that needs no credentials.

post.summary: Ask for write access to a board or a container
post.description: Ask the person for write access to a board, or to one container on it. Ask for the board first: before you write anything on a board you did not create, call this with just `board`. Then, for another agent's container, call it with `board` and `region`. Call it once when `write_board` answers `needs-grant`, naming what that answer names, with a `reason` so the person knows why; then wait for the answer in `check_responses` and resend the same items with the same keys. If you already have an open request for it, that request is returned with `replayed: true`; if you already hold it you get `{ held: true }`.

example.reason: I need to park two notes there.

200.description: An open request already stood, or you already hold the board or container.

201.description: A new grant request was recorded; the person has not answered yet.

board.summary: A request for the whole board

post.description: Write to one board: draw boards, regions, nodes and links, and answer the person with replies, proposals and park bundles. Pass `items` (at most 200), run in order; each item has a `type`: `board`, `region`, `node`, `link`, `unlink`, `reply`, `propose`, `park` or `append`. `append { n, text }` adds text to the end of a node's body as a new version, so you add to a card without rewriting it. Give each item a `key` so a retry never writes twice, and `base` (the version you read) on a node update so a stale edit fails. It answers 200 with one result per item, plus `head` and `pending` (items waiting for your answer). Ask for a board you did not create before writing on it: an item on a board you do not hold fails with `needs-grant` naming the board, and one in another agent's container with `needs-grant` naming the board and region; only a board's creator writes its `board` item again. You cannot decide an item: `propose` acknowledge or drop and the person decides; a proposal made on an older version of the node can't be accepted, so propose again after you change it.

problem.title: Needs a grant
problem.detail: You do not hold the container "later" on board "pricing". Call request_grant once, wait for the person's answer in check_responses, then resend the same items with the same keys.

post.summary: Record one action by the person
post.description: Record one action by the person: acknowledge, drop, comment, ask for context, edit or remove a note not yet sent, save for later, reopen, move, reset, change layout, resize, grant or deny a request, revoke, send, or reject an agent's proposal. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. Pass the board id and the action with its fields. It returns the stored ledger line.

post.summary: Record what the person has seen
post.description: Record that the person has seen a version of a node (`n` and `ver`), so its "updates" badge can clear, or has looked at the board up to a line (`board`, the same board as the path, and `head`, the board's `seq` in `list_boards`), so the board is no longer new or changed. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the stored ledger line.

board.summary: A board, up to a line

get.description: Stream a `change` event with `{ seq }`, the new ledger position, each time anything is appended to the ledger. Only the board page uses it, to know when to reload; agents call `check_responses` with `wait` instead. The connection stays open until the client closes it.

Stream a `change` event with `{ seq }`, the new ledger position, each time anything is appended to the ledger, for every board in the project. It answers on a project with no boards yet, so a client can wait for the first one. When the server runs in watch mode it also sends a `build` event with `{ build }` once on connect and again whenever the page is rebuilt or the server restarts; a client reloads when the value changes. Only the board page uses it; agents call `check_responses` with `wait` instead. The connection stays open until the client closes it.

build.summary: The page being served (watch mode only)

get.description: List the chat sessions on a board, newest first; the first is the one in use. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`.

post.summary: Start a chat session on a board
post.description: Start a new chat session on a board with a command-line agent (`claude` or `kiro`) and, optionally, a model. The new session replaces the board's current one and starts with no memory; starting it is the person's click, so it grants the board to the session's agent. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the session.

post.summary: Send the person's message to the agent
post.description: Send the person's message to the session's agent, with notes (by `seq`) and cards (by number) attached as chips; it also sends the board's round, as the board's Send does. The agent answers on the session's event stream. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the `message_in` event, at once; `conflict` while the agent is still answering.

202.description: The message, as its event; the agent is answering.

post.description: Stop the agent's turn in a session: its process is ended and any approval still waiting is released, denied. The session stays and can take the next message. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns `stopped`, false when nothing was running.

Allow or deny a file change or command the agent is waiting on, `once` (the default) or for the rest of the `session` for that kind of change. The first answer wins: an approval already settled is a `conflict`, and one past its time limit stays denied. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. It returns the `approval_result` event.

200.description: The settled approval, as its event.

get.description: Stream a session's chat events as server-sent `chat` events, each with its `seq` as the event id: first every event after `after`, then each new one as it happens. A client that reconnects passes the last `seq` it saw. Only the board page calls this, with the person's cookie; an agent that calls it is refused with `forbidden`. The connection stays open until the client closes it.

post.summary: Ask the person before a file change or command
post.description: Tell the server, as facts, what the agent is about to change (a file write) or run (a shell command), and wait until it is settled. Only the gate hook of a running chat session calls this, with that session's run token; the person's cookie is refused with `forbidden`. The person is asked unless an answer kept for the session decides; silence past the time limit, a Stop or a new message is a denial. It returns `approved`, and how it was settled.
